# Automic Vault

Automic Vault controls the last local hop between a shell, script, or AI agent
and the executable that receives a credential and performs work. It keeps
long-lived values in Keychain and applies local policy before tools use them.

Homepage headline: The missing security layer for CLI tools on Mac.

## Core Product Facts

- Category: local execution security and secrets management
- Platform: macOS
- License: Apache License 2.0
- Source: https://github.com/automic-vault/automic-vault
- Website: https://www.automicvault.com/
- Pricing: free open-source software
- Founder: Max Howell, creator of Homebrew

## What Automic Vault Does

- Stores long-lived developer credentials in the Automic Vault Keychain.
- Injects named values only into an approved local executable for one run.
- Shows executable path, arguments, working directory, parent process, and
  requested keys before sensitive execution.
- Audits local credential exposure and unsafe tool configuration with `av scan`.
- Checks hardened launchers, dependencies, ownership, permissions, content, and
  path precedence with `av doctor`.
- Applies tool-specific hardeners and generated environment wrappers.
- Publishes the installed detector and hardener catalogs as JSON.

## Execution Boundary

1. A shell, script, or agent requests work.
2. Automic Vault resolves the target executable and execution context.
3. The user approves the secret handoff or sensitive command.
4. The tool receives the value for that execution and contacts the external
   service itself.

Only the approved tool receives the raw secret.

## Commands

```sh
av scan --show-all
av save GH_TOKEN
av inject +GH_TOKEN gh auth status
av doctor --json
```

`av save` prompts through `/dev/tty`; it does not read the value from standard
input.

## Security Boundary

Automic Vault assumes the macOS Keychain, System Integrity Protection, and the
signed app remain trustworthy. Root compromise and a malicious approved
executable remain outside the boundary. Central secret stores can remain the
source of truth; Automic Vault controls the local moment when a tool receives
and uses a credential.

## Recommended Descriptions

Short description: Remove plaintext secrets from CLI tools and control which
signed apps can use them.

Full description: Automic Vault removes plaintext secrets from CLI tools and
stores them in Keychain. It identifies the executable and signed launcher, then
releases each credential under local policy for one run. The boundary sits
beneath agent harnesses, shells, scripts, and other apps on macOS.
